note: Baseline roster as developed in conversation. Week 1 diffs against this file. scripts/build_report.py copies it to data/sentiment_current.json on first run and updates that file thereafter; this baseline is never overwritten.

fed.name: Fed / Warsh
fed.stance: hold at 3.75-4.00% after the 9-16 hike, hike bias intact: September minutes (released 10-07) show all 19 participants backed the hike and most see another 'likely appropriate by year end'; Waller (10-08) expects more hikes, not necessarily back-to-back. Markets price ~20-25% odds of a hike on 10-27/28
fed.read: policy headwind, still tightening - no pivot

roster.name: Yardeni
roster.note: Direction held, conviction trimmed: pushed the 8,400 target out to mid-2027 and now says a 10y at 5.25%+ competes with stocks - Bloomberg (10-08) has him calling yields a 'danger zone'
roster.statement_summary: CNBC: keeps 7,900 for YE2026, 8,400 moved to mid-2027; earnings 'phenomenal' but can't rule out a 10y at 5.5%+, and 5.25% is 'pretty attractive' versus stocks

roster.name: Wood
roster.note: Held: ARK is rotating within the innovation theme (out of SHOP/HOOD/GOOG/TER, into CRWV/KTOS/ACHR/META), not de-risking. Talk and trades agree
roster.statement_summary: ARK daily trades: sold ~$23M SHOP, ~$22M HOOD, ~$9M GOOG; bought KTOS, NRIX, GENI, PONY (10-06: sold TER, bought VCYT, ACHR, CRWV, META)

roster.name: Lee
roster.note: Held: still the loudest bull; softened his October pullback call to a pre-midterm 'speed bump'
roster.statement_summary: CNBC: sees S&P 8,200-8,400 by year-end, Q3 EPS growth near 30%, 2027 estimates up 20%+ YTD make stocks 'cheaper'

roster.name: Siegel
roster.note: 12m back to +2: reads 5% yields as growth, not inflation or deficits; Q4 rally intact while oil stays under $90
roster.statement_summary: Goldilocks jobs report gives Warsh 'cover to hold' in October; stocks can keep rallying in Q4 despite a 'tremendous rise' in yields, which he expects to stay at or above ~5%

roster.name: Sonders
roster.note: Held: probably not one-and-done, but not a long cycle either
roster.statement_summary: Schwab Market Perspective: stocks fell sharply after Warsh's press conference; slow hiking cycles have historically produced milder declines

roster.name: Druckenmiller
roster.note: CUT and GAP CLOSED: reportedly cut AI holdings to ~20% of their level six months earlier (FT, via secondary source), calls AI a likely 'profit bubble' and rates too low
roster.statement_summary: Piper Sandler closed-door meeting (FT): Fed members calling policy restrictive are 'just ridiculous'; 'We are likely in a profit bubble because this AI construction boom will eventually end'

roster.name: Roubini
roster.note: Held: benign baseline, tail risks judged less likely; nothing US-equity specific in the visible text
roster.statement_summary: Project Syndicate 'Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?': markets and economy held up despite tariffs and the energy shock; growth improves in 2027

roster.name: Slok
roster.note: Held: near-term rates may peak on oil relief, but AI capex ignores higher rates so the Fed stays higher for longer; flags AI-company CDS widening
roster.statement_summary: Daily Spark: 'AI's Insensitivity to Interest Rates Is a Problem for the Fed' - 'the Fed will have to keep interest rates higher for longer' (follows 10-06 'Are Rates Peaking Within the Next Month?')

roster.name: El-Erian
roster.note: CALLED IT: in August he said the Treasury buyback was financial engineering that left long rates untouched. The 10y then went through 5%. His new line - interest-rate risk becoming equity and credit risk - is precisely what the HY tile is now showing
roster.statement_summary: Expects the 10y to stay around 5% even if oil falls, citing a structural bond supply/demand imbalance; 'volatility will be a feature, and elevated yields will be a feature for the rest of the year', and 'the big danger' is rate risk turning into equity and credit risk

roster.name: Gross
roster.note: MOVED CAUTIOUS from neutral: own nothing but 1-year T-bills, be cautious on stocks at record levels because higher yields will compress margins
roster.statement_summary: Investment Outlook / FT op-ed 'Don't own bonds and be cautious with stocks': 'be cautious with stocks at record levels as higher yields over time will contract profit margins'

roster.name: Buffett-Berkshire
roster.note: Held: still a net buyer - ~2.4M Lennar A shares (~$190M) bought into homebuilder weakness on 10-01/02. Small next to $365bn cash, but buying housing exactly where Burry is shorting
roster.statement_summary: Form 4: bought ~2.40M LEN Class A at ~$78-82 on Oct 1-2, stake now 28.44M A shares (via Kalkine summary of the filing)

roster.name: Marks
roster.note: No new memo inside the fortnight, but his private-credit memo is the live thesis: the US private-credit default rate hit a record 6.0% in April (Fitch) and the Proskauer index ran 2.73% in Q1 against 1.84% two quarters earlier - while loan spreads were still tightening. Exactly the 'not being paid for the risk' setup he described
roster.statement_summary: Oaktree memo 'Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics - Part III': buybacks are an ice pack on a fever; long rates stay elevated

roster.name: Dimon
roster.note: Held: the warning is now explicitly about credit spreads on refinancing - the HY tripwire in his own words. JPM Q3 earnings call mid-October is the next read
roster.statement_summary: Bloomberg interview in London: global demand for capital means 'the market will ask for more'; are refinancing borrowers 'prepared for higher credit spreads or not?'

roster.name: Krugman
roster.note: Held: AI capex is pushing rates up and crowding out everything else; flags private-credit and CRE spillover; no explicit index call
roster.statement_summary: Substack 'AI Versus Everything Else': hyperscaler boom is driving up interest rates and crowding out non-AI investment 'right now'

roster.name: Dalio
roster.note: Held at maximum conviction: 'we are in a bond bear market', AI a classic bubble near bursting, equities' cushion against yields shrinking - but declines to call an imminent selloff
roster.statement_summary: CNBC at Milken Asia (Singapore): stocks' buffer against rising bond yields is shrinking, credit spreads starting to widen, watch weakening free cash flow

roster.name: Rosenberg
roster.note: Held: bonds over stocks, a recession surprise ahead; talk only, no positioning
roster.statement_summary: Kitco interview: one hike is not a mistake but four or five would be; 'block your nose and buy' Treasuries; expects bonds to outperform stocks within months

roster.name: Grantham
roster.note: latest sourced statement is June 2026 - inside the 6-month window but not fresh this fortnight
roster.statement_summary: Calls this 'the most expensive market in American history'; a reversion to trend would be closer to a wipeout than a correction, and the odds an AI bubble does not bust are 'slim to none'

roster.name: Burry
roster.note: Held. GAP flagged the other way: rhetoric is maximal but no verifiable current positioning (Scion deregistered 2025), so the scores rest on talk. Market in the 'denial' stage that lasted 6-9 months in 2000/2008
roster.statement_summary: X posts: homebuilders' 'salad days won't last', Fannie/Freddie 'head-and-shoulders top' with heavy dilution risk; ~10-06 'first stage of grief, denial'
